title: Denisovans from southwestern China and their subsistence strategies.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the public OSF (Open Science Framework) project pfwnr through its API: 4 files (BFC_lithic_data.xlsx 139 KB, BFC_lithic_analysis.html 6.2 MB, README.html, BFC_OSL_code.txt). Downloaded and parsed the xlsx: sheets Core 187 rows x 36 cols, Flake 221 x 23, Tool 34 x 44, Core fragment & Chunk 924 x 11, plus a Note sheet. Total 1,366 stone artefacts; measurements are length/width/thickness (mm implied) and mass (g implied).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Data availability statement (from the Nature article page): raw data in Supplementary Information and OSF; fossils held at Yunnan Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology. The fossil, faunal, pollen, dating and palaeoproteomic data were not inspected; the supplement was not retrievable (no PMCID, paywalled).

a1_downloadable.note: OSF project is public; the lithic xlsx downloaded without login (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Archaeologist-assigned classes exist as columns (Techno_typology on cores, Techno_type on flakes, Tool_type on tools), seen in the file; they are expert judgements, not measurements.

a3_inputs_present.note: Shape and size measurements and categorical attributes are present per artefact (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Length, Width, Thickness and Mass columns carry no units in the sheet; mm and g are implied by values only (README not read).

a5_enough_rows.note: 1,366 artefacts in total, but the labelled typology classes live on separate sheets with 187 cores, 221 flakes and 34 tools, each far under the ~400 needed for classification; the 924 chunks have only 5 measurements and no typology.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper's full text not accessible to compare counts; no conflicting numbers seen.

a8_label_provenance.note: Techno_type/typology labels are assigned by the analysts largely from the very attributes recorded as features (scar patterns, blank, polarity), so predicting them is partly circular.

backbone.name: none: tabular archaeological measurements, no matching pretrained backbone
backbone.licence: OSF open licence stated for code; data licence not checked

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No standard biological identifiers; artefacts keyed only by excavation specimen numbers.

honest_claim_h3: At best: a classifier reproduces one team's stone-tool typology for ~200 artefacts from one cave, largely from the same attributes used to assign it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use stone-tool measurements to predict the technological category archaeologists assigned to each artefact.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-artefact size, mass, cortex, raw material and flake-scar attributes; 187 cores or 221 flakes (verified counts).
plain_idea.predict: The analyst-assigned category (for example centripetal core, bipolar-on-anvil flake), made by visual inspection rather than measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: the sample is one cave from one team, and the labels are partly defined by the input features.

ml_idea: Classify Bianfu Cave stone artefacts into analyst-assigned technological types from their measurements; rejected for tiny per-class n and circular labels.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 139 KB xlsx parsed in under a second; nothing timed beyond that.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Row count per labelled sheet: 187 cores, 221 flakes, 34 tools (done: fails A5).

verdict_reason: Archaeology paper whose only open table has 1,366 stone artefacts from one cave. The labelled subsets are 187 cores, 221 flakes and 34 tools, all under the A5 minimum. Units are not stated (A4 fail). The tool categories were assigned by the analysts partly from the same attributes we would use as inputs (A8 fail).
